topic: UX Metrics, Analytics, and Data-Driven Design
learningObjectives: Identify UX metrics that measure task success and user behavior.
Interpret basic product analytics for UX decisions.
Distinguish quantitative signals from qualitative evidence.
Connect quantitative findings with qualitative research insights.

activities.title: UX Metrics Map
activities.instruction: Explore how common UX metrics relate to user goals.

content.concept: Metrics such as task completion, conversion rate, retention, error rate, and time on task provide different views of user behavior.
content.tip: Explore each metric and identify the user behavior or outcome it helps measure.

descriptions: Measures how often users successfully complete a task.
Measures the proportion of users who complete a desired action.
Measures how long users take to complete a task.
Measures how frequently users encounter errors.
Measures how many users return over a defined period.
Shows where users leave or abandon a flow.

activities.title: Metric Matcher
activities.instruction: Match each UX question with the most useful metric.

content.concept: The appropriate metric depends on the user behavior or product outcome being investigated.
content.tip: First identify exactly what behavior the UX team wants to measure.

choices: Can users complete the task? → Task Completion Rate
Where do users abandon checkout? → Drop-off Rate
How long does the task take? → Time on Task
How often do users make mistakes? → Error Rate
Do users return to the product? → Retention Rate
config.answer: Can users complete the task? → Task Completion Rate

activities.title: Analytics Explorer
activities.instruction: Adjust the analytics values and observe the UX signal.

content.concept: Behavioral data can reveal where users succeed, hesitate, abandon tasks, or encounter friction.
content.tip: Look for changes in patterns rather than relying on a single number.

activities.title: Insight Synthesis Lab
activities.instruction: Combine quantitative and qualitative evidence into a UX insight.

content.concept: Combining behavioral data with user observations and feedback creates stronger hypotheses about problems and opportunities.
content.tip: Connect the metric signal with an observed user behavior before proposing a design response.
